model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; profit attributable to ordinary shareholders after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2025 actual total operating income (0005.HK_Metrics.csv Revenue; the group's reported top line = net interest income + net fee income + net trading/other income, before operating expenses and ECL). FY2025 is the latest completed fiscal year (Dec year-end); H1 FY2026 (37,742) is the latest interim and is used only to anchor the balance sheet, share count and RoTE trend, not as FY0, because year-1 of the engine (FY2026) must be a full unreported forecast year exactly one year from the valuation date.
inputs.share_count_basis: 17,245m ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (0005.HK_Metrics.csv H1 FY2026 SharesOutstanding), net of treasury/buyback cancellations. Declining materially year over year: 19,983m FY2018 -> 19,600m FY2023 -> 18,485m FY2024 -> 17,547m FY2025 -> 17,245m H1 FY2026, a cumulative ~13.7% reduction since FY2018 funded by cash share repurchases (FY2023 $5,812m, FY2024 $11,348m, FY2025 $9,091m; 0005.HK.duckdb kpis ShareRepurchases). This is NOT an SBC-neutralisation flat count: HSBC's repurchases are real capital return funded from surplus CET1 (the count is modelled declining, unlike NAB.AX/IAG.AX where SBC dilution and buybacks roughly offset). The pace has slowed sharply since the Hang Seng Bank privatisation (completed Jan 2026): buybacks paused for three quarters, then resumed at 'up to $1bn' in 1H26 (0005.HK_Analysis.json guidance) versus the $9-11bn/yr run rate of FY2024-25 -- CET1 fell from 14.9% (end-2025) to 14.1% (1H26) on the privatisation, dividends and RWA growth, leaving much less surplus capital to repurchase against the 14-14.5% target range.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. HSBC is a licensed deposit-taking bank: customer deposits, debt securities in issue and subordinated liabilities are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and balances with central banks are held against that funding (liquidity, not surplus). The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (profit attributable to ordinary shareholders less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt (FY2025 TotalDebt, core_metrics) and cash (FY2025 CashAndEquivalents) are recorded for audit only and play no role in the valuation.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = profit attributable to ordinary shareholders ex-notable-items ~21,650 less capital retained to fund RWA growth at the 14-14.5% CET1 target ~9,400 (~43% retention at FY27 growth of ~5%/12.9% ROTE, see capex_pct_path). Cross-check against realised cash flow: FY2025 net income 21,102 less dividends paid 13,482 and buybacks 9,091 = -1,471 net capital distributed AHEAD of earnings (drawing CET1 down from prior peaks, consistent with the 14.9% end-2025 -> 14.1% 1H26 fall after the Hang Seng deal); FY2024 net income 22,917 less dividends 17,100 and buybacks 11,348 = -5,531, an even larger over-distribution funded by the pre-privatisation capital surplus. The model does NOT assume this pace of over-distribution continues once the post-Hang-Seng CET1 rebuild is underway: base-case retention is set at the growth/ROTE ratio (clean-surplus), materially higher than actual FY2024-25 retention.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +29,766; FY2024 +65,305; H1 FY2026 +81,762) is deposit/loan/trading-asset movement and is not free cash flow to equity; core_metrics OperatingCashFlow is not used in the valuation. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC add-back, consistent with the NAB.AX/IAG.AX bank precedent so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment expense not separately disclosed in the extracted CSV/kpis; FY2023 26 and H1 FY2026 319 appear in 0005.HK_Worksheet.md as contested/notes-section candidates (Annual_FY2023.txt:32188 restricted-share/PSP charge; HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:6648), inconsistent in scale (319 for a half-year vs 26 for a full year suggests one of the two is a different line, e.g. total deferred compensation pool vs P&L charge). Held at an approximate 0.22% of revenue (roughly $150m/yr on ~$68bn revenue), immaterial either way for a bank whose flow is dominated by NII and credit costs -- the house/street band this produces is narrow and does not drive the valuation.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income is the core of the banking business (gross interest income and net interest income, kpis GrossInterestIncome/NetInterestIncome) and is fully inside the modelled revenue and margin path; no separate cash balance is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction, as for NAB.AX/IAG.AX).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 cash buybacks $9,091m (0005.HK.duckdb kpis ShareRepurchases), down from FY2024's $11,348m peak. H1 FY2026 shows $0 in the kpis table (buybacks were paused through most of 1H26 pending the Hang Seng privatisation completion in January 2026 and resumed only within the half at 'up to $1bn', per 0005.HK_Analysis.json guidance -- the $1bn tranche may not yet be reflected in the extracted H1 filing's cash flow statement). The declining share count (projected_shares) is the model's mechanism for capital return via repurchase; buyback_cash is recorded for audit only and does not separately reduce equity value in the FCFE engine.
inputs.fx_note: HSBC reports and files in USD (0005.HK_Metrics.csv Currency=USD); its primary listing (0005.HK) quotes in HKD, pegged to USD within a narrow band under Hong Kong's currency board (target range 7.75-7.85 HKD/USD since 1983). fx_rate 7.8431 = HKD per USD (1 / 0.1275, the Yahoo Finance HKDUSD=X cross of 0.1275 as of 2026-09-25), matching the engine's convention that fx_rate is quote-currency units per unit of model currency (confirmed against PRU.AX USD-model/AUD-quote fx_rate 1.4253 = AUD per USD, and WISE.L USD-model/GBp-quote fx_rate 74.8391 = pence per USD). Because the peg is effectively fixed within its band, currency risk between the model (USD) and quote (HKD) is minimal and no separate risk premium is added for it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows and the group's functional/presentation currency: US 10-year Treasury ~4.1% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.05 x global equity risk premium 5.5% = 9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. Beta set slightly above 1.0 (versus NAB.AX/IAG.AX domestic banks at 1.0) to reflect HSBC's multi-jurisdictional regulatory/geopolitical risk (US-China tensions, sanctions exposure, Hong Kong/China concentration) even though its funding base (sticky Hong Kong retail/commercial deposits) is arguably more stable than a domestic-only bank's. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle (Hong Kong CRE), geopolitical and execution risk (multi-country divestiture programme) is charged in the bear flows and the bear weight, not stacked as a further premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial relative to a ~$3.2 trillion balance sheet and not separately disclosed at group level in the extracted data; lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. The revenue and margin path is built on profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders (0005.HK_Metrics.csv NetIncome, which ties to reported basic EPS: FY2025 21,102/17,547 = $1.20, matching reported EPS 1.20), which already nets out both non-controlling interests and AT1/preference dividend coupons (the gap to the separately-reported NPAT KPI, e.g. FY2025 NPAT 23,131 vs NetIncome 21,102, a ~$2.0bn difference consistent with AT1 coupons plus minority interests). No further NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T08:08:12Z HKEX regular close (per Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketTime); 52-week range HKD 100.40-169.70.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the validated component engine (dcf_engine.py), following the NAB.AX (2026-09-24) and IAG.AX (2026-09-23) precedent -- SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book, and FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent, which goes through the slider engine and also produces the workbook. Engine mapping: revenue = total operating income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax profit margin (operating income - operating expenses - ECL charge) PLUS the SBC add-back, as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path = 0.22%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation/amortisation sits inside operating expenses, a genuine cost for a bank, not an add-back); capex_pct_path = capital retained to fund RWA growth at the CET1 target = NPAT margin x g/ROTE; cash_tax_rate_path = effective tax rate on profit before tax to profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (includes NCI/AT1 leakage); wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0. FY0 reconciliation: FY2025 actual pre-tax-margin build: ProfitBeforeTax 29,907 / Revenue 68,274 = 43.8%; NetIncome 21,102 / Revenue 68,274 = 30.9% (this 30.9% is the post-tax, post-NCI, post-AT1 margin the engine's capex/retention math should approximately reproduce net of the modelled retention). DATA GAPS (per financial-parser's note): FY2024, FY2025, H1-2024 and H1-2025 have missing ROE, cost/income, NAV/NTA-per-share and RWA cells from OCR gaps on key-metrics pages; used what is populated (RWA FY2025 888,647; FY2025 CTI missing but FY2023 48.5%, H1 FY2025 49.9%, H1 FY2026 46.2% bracket it) and did not force-fill gaps. IFRS 4/IFRS 17 boundary: FY2021 and earlier used the old insurance accounting standard; FY2022 onward is IFRS 17-restated, so pre/post-2022 revenue and margin are not strictly like-for-like -- the growth-rate selection below deliberately weights the FY2022-2025 (IFRS 17, post-COVID) window and management's own FY2026-28 guidance over the full 7-year CAGR for this reason. Definitional gap flagged: management's FY2026 guidance of 'banking NII at least $46bn' does not tie directly to the reported P&L net interest income line (FY2025 34,794 per kpis/CSV) -- banking NII is a broader internally-defined measure (includes NII from Markets Treasury / structural hedge income booked outside the retail/commercial net interest margin line) that HSBC does not reconcile to statutory NII in the extracted disclosures. The growth path below is built off reported total operating income (the reconcilable, audited figure), not the unreconciled banking-NII guidance number, to avoid overstating the base.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blend of FY2022-25 (post-IFRS-17, post-COVID) revenue trend and management's FY2026-28 guidance (year-on-year growth rising to 5% in 2028 vs 2027), tapering toward the 7-year 3.5% CAGR at terminal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (0.2%) and 3-year (2.2%) diverge sharply from revenue (6.2%/10.5%) and especially EPS (44.6%/18.6%): equity/book value is held almost flat because HSBC distributes close to (and in FY2024-25, more than) 100% of earnings via dividends (50% payout target) plus large buybacks ($9-11bn/yr FY2024-25), so equity CAGR does not describe earnings power and is NOT used as the growth anchor -- unlike the default 'value investing' preference in Step 1c, which would be wrong for a bank returning capital by design. EPS CAGRs are inflated by the FY2020 COVID/rate-trough base (EPS $0.19) and further amplified by the shrinking share count; neither the 5-year (44.6%, trough-to-peak) nor even the 3-year (18.6%, still off a depressed FY2022 base) figure is a repeatable trend. Revenue (total operating income) is the cleanest anchor and is what the growth path uses.

bear.growth_rationale: A faster global rate-cutting cycle than management's guidance basis pressures banking NII (the single largest risk flagged in 0005.HK_Analysis.json: 'NII guidance ... depends on market-implied interest rates and structural hedge reinvestment; a faster-than-expected rate-cutting cycle would pressure banking NII'), Hong Kong/China property stress keeps ECL elevated, and the multi-country divestiture programme (Egypt, Türkiye, Indonesia, Australia, Malta, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) shrinks the revenue base as businesses are sold rather than replaced with growth. Total operating income grows just 0.5-1.5%.
bear.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin + SBC on revenue. FY2025 actual pre-tax margin was 43.8% (ProfitBeforeTax 29,907/Revenue 68,274) on a benign ECL year; the bear case assumes ECL rises toward the top of the medium-term 30-40bps planning range (management guided ~45bps for FY2026 already, before a downturn) and cost growth outpaces a shrinking/rate-pressured revenue base as the ~$2.0bn simplification programme's savings are consumed by inflation and continued conduct/regulatory spend: 37.0% initially, recovering modestly to 39.0% as divestitures complete and the cost base resets lower alongside the smaller revenue base.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin (~26% post-tax) x g / ROTE 10.5% (bear case RoTE well below the 17%+ guidance, reflecting elevated ECL and rate pressure). Even at low 0.5-1.5% growth, capital must be retained to rebuild CET1 toward the 14-14.5% target after the Hang Seng-driven drawdown (14.9% end-2025 -> 14.1% 1H26), so retention does not collapse to zero the way it would for a pure growth-driven bank.

base.growth_rationale: Total operating income. FY2026 3.0% and FY2027 3.5% follow management's own guidance ('year-on-year growth 2026-2028, rising to 5% growth in 2028 vs 2027') applied to the reconcilable reported-revenue base rather than the unreconciled 'banking NII >=$46bn' figure; ramps to 4.0-4.5% as the Hang Seng synergies ($0.5-0.9bn by 2028), Asia wealth momentum (18% cc growth, $64bn net new money in 1H26) and the surging Hong Kong IPO pipeline (~40 deals in 2026 vs 5 in 2025, per 0005.HK_Analysis.json) come through CIB and wealth fee income, then tapers to a 2.5% terminal rate in line with the 7-year 3.5% CAGR and long-run nominal global GDP-linked bank growth.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin + SBC on revenue. FY2025 actual was 43.8%; base case assumes the ~$2.0bn simplification programme (raised from $1.5bn, ~$1.7bn already actioned per 1H26) continues to outpace ~1% YoY target-basis opex growth guidance, ECL normalises toward the medium-term 30-40bps planning range (below FY2026's guided ~45bps, which includes held-for-sale portfolios), and Hang Seng/Asia-pivot synergies lift margin from 42.0% (FY2026, still absorbing restructuring costs) to a steady-state 46.0% by the back half of the decade -- broadly consistent with the RoTE-ex-notables trajectory already visible in 1H26 (19.1%).
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 within the 14-14.5% target as RWA grows with the balance sheet = post-tax margin (~29-30%) x g / RoTE-ex-notables target of ~14-15% (management guides '17% or better' RoTE, but that measure nets AT1 coupons differently and the engine's ROTE-equivalent on ordinary-shareholder profit runs somewhat below the headline target; 14-15% is a conservative read consistent with 1H26's 18.2% reported / 19.1% ex-notables translating to a lower figure once averaged over a full cycle including weaker halves). At FY2026's 3.0% growth this retains ~35% of post-tax profit (65% distributed via dividends + buybacks, close to but below headline 50% dividend-only payout, i.e. buybacks are additive as modelled through the declining share count); at 2.5% terminal growth only ~18% is retained (82% distributed).

bull.growth_rationale: Simplification and Asia-pivot execution beats plan (RoTE ex-notables already 19.1% in 1H26 against a 17%+ target), Hang Seng synergies land at the top of the $0.5-0.9bn range, the Hong Kong IPO boom (~40 deals pipeline) sustains CIB/capital-markets fee income, and Asia wealth net-new-money momentum ($64bn in 1H26, $57bn from Asia) compounds as HSBC's wealth centres and relationship-manager build-out scale. Total operating income grows 5-6% through the medHong Kong-driven growth years, tapering to 3.5% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Simplification savings land ahead of the $2.0bn target with limited re-investment leakage, ECL stays benign (below the 30bps floor of the medium-term range as the Hong Kong CRE cycle turns), and the divested lower-return franchises (Türkiye, Egypt, Indonesia, Australia retail, Malta, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) leave a structurally higher-margin remaining book concentrated in Hong Kong/Asia wealth and CIB: 45.0% rising to a 51.0% steady state.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = post-tax margin (~32-33%) x g / RoTE ~17% (bull case actually achieves the headline 17%+ guidance sustainably). Higher growth needs proportionally more retained capital even at a superior return; terminal 3.5% growth still retains ~20% (80% distributed via dividend + accelerated buybacks).

scenario_narratives.base: HSBC's revenue grows 3-4.5% as the Elhedery-era simplification programme (targeting ~$2.0bn of annualised savings, already $1.7bn actioned) funds reinvestment in Hong Kong, Asia wealth and CIB while the multi-country retail divestiture programme (Egypt, Türkiye review, Indonesia, Australia, Malta, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) trims the lower-return tail. Pre-tax margin recovers from 42% to a 46% steady state as cost discipline outpaces a modest, guided revenue ramp and ECL normalises toward the 30-40bps medium-term range. At a 10.0% USD cost of equity and capital retained to hold CET1 within the 14-14.5% target, the franchise is worth what the engine implies against a market price that already reflects strong recent execution (1H26 RoTE ex-notables 19.1%).
scenario_narratives.bull: Simplification and the Asia pivot beat plan: Hang Seng synergies land at the top of guidance, the Hong Kong IPO boom (~40 deals pipeline vs 5 in 2025) sustains CIB fee income, and Asia wealth net-new-money momentum compounds. Revenue grows 5-6% tapering to 3.5%, pre-tax margin reaches 51%, and RoTE sustainably clears the 17%+ guidance range.
scenario_narratives.bear: A faster global rate-cutting cycle than management's guidance basis pressures banking NII, Hong Kong/China property stress keeps commercial-real-estate ECL elevated above the guided 45bps, and the multi-country divestiture programme shrinks the revenue base faster than cost savings or replacement growth can offset -- while ongoing geopolitical friction (US-China tensions, sanctions exposure, Hong Kong political risk) sits as a standing overhang management cannot fully control. Revenue growth slows to 0.5-1.5% and margin recovery stalls near 39%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 adjusted: bear raised to 25% given HSBC's structural exposure to two risks largely outside management's control simultaneously -- interest-rate-cycle sensitivity on banking NII (the single largest guided revenue driver) and Hong Kong/China political and property-market risk (profit is heavily concentrated there), compounded by real execution risk across seven concurrent country divestitures. Bull trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default): at 1H26 RoTE ex-notables already at 19.1% against a 17%+ target, much of the near-term upside from simplification execution is plausibly already priced in, and the bull case requires that execution AND the rate/credit cycle AND the divestiture programme all continue running favourably for a decade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A global bank is valued on what it can distribute to ordinary shareholders after funding regulatory capital (CET1) needed to support risk-weighted-asset growth, discounted at a USD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow (deposit/loan/trading movement) and never with deposits, debt securities in issue or subordinated liabilities treated as net debt. Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (net of NCI and AT1 coupons, tying to reported EPS) is the flow; capital retention to hold the 14-14.5% CET1 target is the reinvestment; 10.0% is the USD return an owner requires, set modestly above the 9.7% used for NAB.AX/IAG.AX to reflect HSBC's added multi-jurisdictional regulatory and geopolitical risk. The result is the FCFE-clean-surplus equivalent of a residual-income-on-tangible-book answer: value scales with (RoTE - g)/(CoE - g) against tangible book, and the model does not assume the aggressive FY2024-25 pace of capital distribution (which briefly ran ahead of organic capital generation and pulled CET1 down from 14.9% to 14.1%) continues indefinitely.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate cycle: banking NII is management's single largest guided revenue driver and explicitly flagged as rate-sensitive; a faster-than-priced global cutting cycle compresses margin directly

Hong Kong/China concentration: the majority of group profit derives from Hong Kong and mainland China; property-sector stress, a Chinese growth slowdown or Hong Kong political/economic disruption disproportionately hits earnings and is not diversifiable away within the model

Credit losses: 1H26 ECL of $2.4bn (up from $2.0bn in 1H25) includes a $0.4bn fraud-related UK securitisation exposure and continuing Hong Kong CRE stress; FY2026 guided at ~45bps of average gross loans, above the 30-40bps medium-term planning range

Execution risk on the seven concurrent divestitures (Egypt, Türkiye review, Indonesia, Australia retail, Malta, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) plus Hang Seng integration -- any could slip, disappoint, or incur unbudgeted restructuring cost

Geopolitical and regulatory: HSBC sits structurally between the Chinese and Western financial systems, exposing it to sanctions, AML/CTF enforcement, and Hong Kong national-security-law dynamics across ~57 jurisdictions simultaneously

Capital return pace: FY2024-25 distributions (dividends + buybacks) ran ahead of organic capital generation, drawing CET1 from 14.9% to 14.1%; the model assumes a materially slower buyback pace than FY2024-25's $9-11bn/yr as the post-Hang-Seng CET1 rebuild continues, and a return to the prior aggressive pace (upside to per-share value) or a further capital-rebuild-driven slowdown (downside) are both plausible

Data completeness: FY2024, FY2025, H1-2024 and H1-2025 carry OCR-driven gaps in ROE, cost-to-income, NAV/NTA-per-share and RWA in the source CSV; the model used what was populated and did not interpolate missing cells

IFRS 4/IFRS 17 boundary: FY2021-and-earlier figures are on the old insurance accounting standard, not strictly comparable to FY2022+ IFRS-17-restated figures, so long-run (7-year) CAGRs mix two accounting bases

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range recorded in inputs.price_as_of.
data_sources.financials: 0005.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, FY2018-FY2025 annual + H1 FY2024/H1 FY2025/H1 FY2026) exported from 0005.HK.duckdb; kpis table for NetInterestIncome, GrossInterestIncome, ProfitBeforeTax, NPAT, CashTaxesPaid, DividendsPaid, ShareRepurchases, Depreciation, CET1Ratio, CostToIncomeRatio, CreditImpairmentCharge, NIM, NAVPerShare, NTAPerShare, ROE, ROTE, RiskWeightedAssets; 0005.HK_Worksheet.md for the adjudication trail and stock-based-comp candidates.
data_sources.qualitative: 0005.HK_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): Elhedery-era simplification and Asia pivot, Hang Seng Bank privatisation (completed Jan 2026), 1H26 RoTE 18.2% (19.1% ex-notables), CET1 14.1%, FY2026-28 guidance (RoTE 17%+, revenue growth to 5% by 2028, 50% dividend payout, banking NII >=$46bn, ECL ~45bps, target opex growth ~1%, CET1 14-14.5%, up to $1bn resumed buyback), bull/bear cases and risk taxonomy.
